 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 164 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 2-9-2024 at about 2.50 p.m., Sumithramma as a pedestrian, was crossing Bengaluru- Mysore road and when she reached near TTMC Bus stand, Kengeri, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AD-6953 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Sumithramma, result of which Sumithramma was thrown to the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately Sumithramma was shifted to H.K. Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Rajarajeshwari hospital, but on the way to the hospital, she was succumbed to the accidental injuries.
The petitioners have spent Rs.50,000/- towards hospitalization and other incidental charges and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards final rites of the deceased.
3. Prior to the accident, Sumithramma was hale and healthy.
She was aged about 70 years.
She was Home maker.
Due to the untimely death of deceased, petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/the RC owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AD- 6953 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex- parte.

5. The Respondent no.2/the Insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AD-6953 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 contended that the petitioner no.2 is the married daughter and petitioner no.1 is the major son of the deceased and he is the earning Upendra A vs Meena K on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188597522/
2 member hence, petitioners are not the dependents of the deceased and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased herself and that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle.

sentences.text:
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 2-9- 2024 at about 2.50 p.m. near TTMC bus stop, Kengeri, Mysore road, Bengaluru, due to the use and involvement of the car bearing reg.No.KA-04-AD-6953?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3
. What order or Award ?
7. The petitioner No.1 got examined himself as Pw1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
On the other side, the Respondent No.2 did not adduce evidence on its behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- It is contended by the petitioners that

on 2-9-2024 at about 2.50 p.m.,
Sumithramma (hereinafter called as deceased) as a pedestrian, was crossing Bengaluru-Mysore road and when she reached near TTMC Bus stand, Kengeri, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AD-6953 (here in after called the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, result of which she was thrown to the road and sustained grievous injuries and on the way to the hospital, she was succumbed to the accidental injuries 11.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the son of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 11 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.10 i.e.,F.I.R with complaint, Police memo, Crime details form, Sketch, Inquest mahazar, Notice U/sec. 133 of M.V.
Act, PM report, IMV report, confession statement of accused, charge sheet etc.,
Upendra A vs Meena K on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188597522/
3 12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the daughter of deceased by name Veena, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 151/2024 of Kengeri Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 106 of B.N.S 2023.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 281, 106 of B.N.S 2023.
13.

The respondent no. 2 in their written statement and evidence has categorically contended that the accident in question was due to the sole negligence of the petitioner but not of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, submitted to dismiss the petition.

14. It is not in dispute that petitioner has filed this petition u/Sec.164 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.
If the claim petition is filed u/Sec.164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the petitioner need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It is sufficient if they prove the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries and death of the deceased.

15. The Learned counsel for respondent no.2 has vehemently argued that, though the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle on the allegation that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the cause for the accident but the petitioners instead of filing the claim petition u/Sec. 166 IMV Act have opted to file the petition u/Sec. 164 of IMV Act for the reason that deceased is aged lady and if claim petition is filed u/Sec. 166 IMV Act the claimants will get meager amount and if claim petition is filed u/Sec. 164 of IMV Act they will get fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

It is further submitted that when there is specific provision provided under the Motor Vehicles Act, the petitioners have to file petition u/Sec. 166 of IMV Act,
hence, present petition is not maintainable hence on that count itself the petition is liable to be dismissed.
16.

The Learned counsel in further has submitted that the deceased during her life time was residing separately in the address given in the Aadhar card and petitioner no.1 and 2 are residing separately and the petitioners have not produced any document to prove that deceased was residing with them.
17. So far as the maintainability of petition is concerned, the petitioners being the legal heirs of deceased have filed claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act.

If either Sec. 166 of IMV Act or Sec.
164 of IMV Act is read nowhere there is any bar raised to file the petition either u/Sec. 166 IMV Act or U/Sec. 164 of the IMV Act.

The claimant has the option to choose to file a claim petition u/Sec.
164 or 166 of the MV Act.
Sec. 164 is a no fault provision where negligence need not be proved.
While Sec. 166 requires proof of the driver's negligence and is a claim based on fault.
The choice depends on the claimant's ability to prove negligence and the income of the victim.

18. In a decision reported in ILR 2008 KAR 1249 in the case of Oriental Insurance Co, Ltd. Vs Salma and others Hon'ble lordships have held that;
"a petition under section 163A of the act is maintainable even in case where negligence is on the part of the victim"

4 19.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2004) 5 SCC 385 rendered in Deepal Girihsbhai Soni and Ors Vs United India Insurance co, ltd., held that;
"Section 163A also covers the cases where negligence is even on the part of the victim held excluding the defense of contributory negligence".

entities.text: Deepal Girihsbhai Soni and Ors Vs United India Insurance co, ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. In the present case, if the police records are perused, more particular the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the deceased as pedestrian while crossing the road met with an accident as the offending vehicle hit against her.

21. In view of the above provision of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 164 of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered is whether vehicle against which the claim is made is involved in the accident.
In this case, it is pertinent to note that nowhere in the written statement the Respondents have denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

22. Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P10, this court is of the opinion that the accident was due to the involvement or use of the offending vehicle and in that the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.2:- Admittedly this petition is filed u/Sec.164 of IMV Act.

Sec. 164 of MV Act reads as follows:
"164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc.- (1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.
(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section".
24.
As per Sec.164 of MV Act petitioners are entitled for fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

Upendra A vs Meena K on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188597522/
5 25.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
26. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compen- sation of Rs.5,00,000/- + cost of Rs.1000/- imposed vide order on IA No.II & III.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.5,01,000/- (Rupees Five Lakh One Thou- sand only).
A Sum of Rs.5,00,000/- shall also carry inter- est at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensa- tion and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.2,50,500/- each.

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners No.1 and 2 on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 3rd day of October 2025.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
